what: Class-level lifetimes of US Google Trends 'Trending now' searches over their first 24 hours, from a year of twice-daily reads: for the P6 survival prior and the C7 amendment. No per-trend names or times.

source.name: Trends Story (oopus)
source.collected: US Google Trends 'Trending now', past-24-hour list, read through SerpAPI at 5:00 and 16:00 US Eastern
source.span: reads 2025-10-21 to 2026-10-18 (the 12 earlier reads carry a clock 12 h or more off and are left out)

built_by: scratchpad trends-story analysis (Python NPMLE, node back-test on lib/forecast)
class: P6's: group (pop: categories 2, 4, 6, 8; sports: 17; other) x volume band at the trend's newest read (5K, 20K, 100K+; lt5K for reference, never forecast)
end: Trends Story stores GT's 'active' flag at each read, not an end time: a life is the interval between the last read active and the first read not active (Turnbull NPMLE, 10-minute grid, no truncation: the 24 h list shows ended searches too, so it samples by start). This is GT's FIRST end. Against our own Trends replies over the same weeks, 10-17% of reads of 5K+ searches aged 6-24 h say ended while GT later moves the end on (median 4.7 h): for the 5K and 20K classes S at 12 h runs 0.09-0.16 below P6's Kaplan-Meier (100K classes: -0.01 to 0.10). Use as a lower bound on GT's final end, not a substitute.

best_single_number_p6_final_end.note: From P6's Kaplan-Meier (78 replies, 4 countries, final ends, followed to 168 h): the most any single number per class can score if the class curve were known exactly. [max share within +-50%, the number that gets it, min median error (h), mass past the data]. In-sample, so optimistic.
best_single_number_p6_final_end.both_at_once: Checked at every even age 2-48 h (30+ lives reaching it): one number holds <= 8 h median error and >= 50% within +-50% only for pop/5K at 38 h old (51.9%) and sports/5K at 24-26 h old (50.4-51.1%); never at the far edge of a 95% interval. Best share within +-50% over all ages: pop/5K 0.52, pop/20K 0.48, pop/100K 0.72, sports/5K 0.51, sports/20K 0.46, sports/100K 0.44, other/5K 0.50, other/20K 0.54, other/100K 0.58.

chance_still_on_next_read.target: GT still marks it active at the next read, 11-13 h later (Trends Story reads), given active now and 2-14 h old

backtest.design_note: P6's own code (lib/forecast/backtest.js, score.js) on the same 78 saved Trends replies; only the model's curve changes. 'with': per class, S on 0-24 h is the Turnbull NPMLE of the P6 lives cut at 24 h plus every Trends Story interval read by the moment (never later); past 24 h, the P6 lives' Kaplan-Meier given 24 h (the likelihood factorises there). Baselines from P6 lives only. A 0.25 h grid; the grid alone (no Trends Story) reproduces P6: 45 shown, 11.5 h, 31%, IQR 36% (P6: 11.0 h, 31%, 36%).

weekly_recurrence_rule.rule: A search is 'weekly' when the same query (case-folded) started trending within +-12 h of 7, 14, 21 or 28 days before, in at least 2 of those 4 weeks.
weekly_recurrence_rule.chosen_on: starts 2025-11-19 to 2026-06-23, 5K+, by lift among rules firing on 1% or more

weekly_excess.note: share of 5K+ trends whose query trended at a whole number of weeks before (+-12 h, 1-4 weeks) minus the share at half-week lags

weekly_queries.definition: 3+ gaps between its trends within 12 h of a whole number of weeks, and at least half its gaps so
